BURSEVI:v10p254/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p254/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p254/r5.claim: Hell is the unbelieving transgressor’s permanent abode; believers who sin may leave it, so the passage addresses disbelievers while warning other readers.
BURSEVI:v10p254/r5.anchor: فالكلام في حق الكافر لكن فيه موعظة وعبرة موقظة واللام سادة مسد الإضافة

QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.claim: Transgressors exceed human nature’s balance toward animal or predatory ranks and prefer sensory pleasure to real life, so hell becomes their home.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.anchor: تعدى طور الفطرة الإنسانية وجاوز حد العدالة والشريعة إلى الرتبة البهيمية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r4.claim: The phrase ‘Hell shall be his abode’ emphasizes that transgressors will remain in Hell forever with no other place to go.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p166/r4.anchor: they will abide in Hell forever

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r2.claim: Basran grammar supplies an omitted pronoun, المأوى له; the Kufans treat ال as replacing it. Al-Zamakhshari gives فإن الجحيم مأواه, but Abu Hayyan finds no subject-predicate link in his analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r2.anchor: والعائد على من من الخبر محذوف على رأي البصريين، أي المأوى له

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r3.claim: Hell is the tyrant’s refuge; the definite article substitutes for a possessive, and هي may be a separator or subject.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r3.anchor: { فإن الجحيم هى المأوى } هي مأواه واللام فيه سادة مسد الإضافة

BINTSHATI:v1p155/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r2.claim: Al-Jahīm names a fiercely blazing fire; the religious term preserves its lexical sense of intense ignition.
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r2.anchor: فالجحيم والجحمة في اللغة: النار الشديدة التأجج

BINTSHATI:v1p157/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r1.claim: Qur’anic āwā can mean granting refuge and can also describe hoped-for or imagined refuge, as the cited examples show.
BINTSHATI:v1p157/r1.anchor: وإما على سبيل الرجاء أو الوهم

NAHHAS:v5p146/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p146/r8.claim: Kufans parse fa-hiya maʾwāhu, with alif replacing a pronoun; Basrans parse hiya al-maʾwā lahu.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r8.anchor: والتقدير عند الكوفيين فهي مأواه والألف بدل من الضمير والتقدير عند البصريين هي المأوى له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r2.speaker: البصريون
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r2.claim: The Basran grammatical analysis supplies an omitted pronoun after hiya in the phrase meaning that Hell is the abode for the transgressor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r2.anchor: هذا مذهب البصريين أن الضمير محذوف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r3.claim: The Kufan analysis makes the definite article al stand in for the omitted pronoun, an analysis Abū Ḥayyān attributes to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r3.anchor: وعند الكوفيين أن ( أل ) نائب عن الضمير قاله أبو حيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.claim: The blame concerns choosing worldly life over the afterlife; worldly benefits that do not cost one the afterlife are not blameworthy, as the counsel to Qarun shows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2.anchor: فأما الأخذ بحظوظ الحياة الدنيا التي لا يفيت الأخذ بها حظوظ الآخرة فذلك غير مذموم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.claim: المأوى is the dwelling where someone settles and remains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2.anchor: والمأوى والمسكن حيث يأوي المرء ويلازم

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.claim: Choosing worldly life over the Hereafter is blameworthy, whereas choosing the Hereafter is praiseworthy.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.anchor: فمن آثر الدنيا على الآخرة فهو مذموم، ومن آثر الآخرة فهو ممدوح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.claim: The response after فإذا is ‘then the matter is as follows’; الجحيم هي المأوى means Hell is his abode, with a known possessor understood rather than expressed, and هي is either a separator or subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1.anchor: أي : فإذا جاءت الطاقة فإن الأمر كذلك

MUQATIL:79:34-41/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r7.claim: The transgressor is fixed in shirk, chooses worldly life over the next, does not fear God or judgment, and consumes what is forbidden; Hell is his abode.
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r7.anchor: { فأما من طغى } الثابت على الشرك، وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r6.claim: The Fire is the person's refuge; the definite article in al-maʾwā stands in place of the possessive pronoun.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r6.anchor: أي مأواه. والألف واللام بدل من الهاء.

ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r2.claim: Some take the article al- as replacing the possessive pronoun, so al-maʾwā means “his refuge”; the vocative command “lower the gaze, man” likewise means “your gaze,” as in the poet’s line.
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: الألف واللام بدل من الهاء، المعنى فهي مأواه

ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.claim: The poet’s “lower the gaze” addresses a man whose gaze is meant; this supports reading al-maʾwā as “his refuge” for both Hell and Paradise.
ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: فغض الطرف إنك من نمير. . . فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا

RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.claim: After describing Resurrection generally, God divides those morally responsible into wretched and blessed, beginning with the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.anchor: قسم المكلفين قسمين : الأشقياء والسعداء ، فذكر حال الأشقياء

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.claim: Transgression entails rejecting the afterlife, preferring worldly life, and following the self's desires; the opposite is fear that restrains attachment to the world and forbids following desire.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.anchor: كان لما يقابل الطغيان من الوصف وهو الخوف ما يقابل الإيثار واتباع هوى النفس

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.claim: The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.anchor: وهناك غير الطائفتين طوائف أخر من المستضعفين والذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.claim: In “the refuge,” the definite article can replace a possessive pronoun, or an omitted pronoun can be supplied: it means the refuge for him.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r4.anchor: على أن تكون اللام عوضا عن الضمير أو الضمير محذوف والتقدير هي المأوى له

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.claim: These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.anchor: Bu birkaç kısa âyette âhiretteki büyük kaybı veya büyük kurtuluşu hazırlayan olumsuz ve olumlu tutumların çok veciz bir özeti yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r4.claim: Verse 39 reminds these people of their bad end.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r4.anchor: İşte 39. âyette bunların kötü âkıbeti hatırlatılmaktadır

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.claim: Rāzī infers that the sinner who lacks these two defining traits is not described as having Hell for his permanent abode.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9.anchor: وتخصيصه بهذه الحالة يدل على أن الفاسق الذي لا يكون كذلك ، لا تكون الجحيم مأوى له

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r10.claim: The phrase may elide له after al-maʾwā because the meaning is clear, as in the command lower your gaze; Rāzī also reads it as the fitting abode for such a person.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r10.anchor: ثم حذفت الصلة لوضوح المعنى كقولك للرجل غض الطرف

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.claim: Together, intellectual and practical corruption represent the greatest corruption and merit eternal punishment; Hell is the refuge for those reaching this level.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.anchor: The two together are thus taken to indicate the greatest degree of corruption, the punishment for which is eternal

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r5.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r5.claim: Those who do not reach this level may still be punished, but Hell will not be their ultimate refuge.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r5.anchor: Those who do not may still be punished, but Hellfire will not be their ultimate refuge (R)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r1.claim: Al-maʾwā is the place that shelters or receives him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Hell is the abode of whoever has this description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي هي: المأوى) (¬9) لمن كان

BURHAN:v4p37/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.claim: The definite article can stand in for a pronoun: Hell is its refuge for the one who preferred worldly life, while Paradise is the refuge for the one who feared God.
BURHAN:v4p37/r4.anchor: فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى

BURHAN:v4p37/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.claim: The Kufans explain the definite article in these refuge phrases as a substitute for the omitted pronoun.
BURHAN:v4p37/r5.anchor: وقول الكوفيين الألف واللام عوض من الضمير

BURHAN:v4p334/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p334/r1.claim: The Kufans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is his refuge.’
BURHAN:v4p334/r1.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الإضمار بعدها مراد وإنما اختلفوا في تقديره فعند الكوفيين هي مأواه

BURHAN:v4p334/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r2.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v4p334/r2.claim: The Basrans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is the refuge for him.’

BURHAN:v4p334/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p334/r3.claim: The article’s lām is normally light; in the name Allah it is emphatic after a preceding fatḥa or ḍamma, conveying reverence for God.
BURHAN:v4p334/r3.anchor: واللام في التعريف مرققة إلا في اسم الله فيجب تفخيمها إذا كان قبلها ضمة أو فتحة وهي في الأسماء تفخيم الجرس وفي المعنى توقير المسمى وتعظيمه سبحانه

BURHAN:v4p334/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p334/r4.claim: The lām in demonstrative names signals distance or reinforces it; grammarians differ on which function it has.
BURHAN:v4p334/r4.anchor: والدالة على البعد الداخلة على أسماء الإشارة إعلاما بالبعد أو توكيدا له على الخلاف فيه

BURHAN:v4p334/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p334/r5.claim: With weakened inna, the lām is called the initial or differentiating lām because it distinguishes the affirmative particle from negative inna and confirms the predicate.
BURHAN:v4p334/r5.anchor: وتسمى لام الابتداء والفارقة لأنها تفرق بينها وبين إن النافية والمخففة هي التي تحقق الخبر مع المبتدأ

BURHAN:v4p334/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r6.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p334/r6.claim: The Kufans take lām to mean ‘except’ in affirmative clauses, with inna meaning ‘not’; al-Kisa’i reads the verb with the nominative on this basis.

BURHAN:v4p334/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r7.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v4p334/r7.claim: Al-Kisa’i reads ‘to make the mountains disappear’ in the nominative and understands the clause as ‘their plot was only intended to make them disappear.’
BURHAN:v4p334/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ﴿ وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال ﴾ 6 بالرفع

BURHAN:v4p334/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p334/r8.claim: Emphatic lām can precede a subject or occur with inna on a delayed subject or predicate; inna emphasizes what follows and lām emphasizes the predicate.
BURHAN:v4p334/r8.anchor: أحدهما المبتدأ وتسمى لام الابتداء فيؤذن بأنه المحكوم

BURHAN:v4p334/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r9.speaker: سعيد
BURHAN:v4p334/r9.claim: Sa‘id reads the hamza of inna open in ‘they surely eat’; the author explains that its lām is licensed only with kasra-inna or with a fronted predicate.
BURHAN:v4p334/r9.anchor: وكذا في إن المفتوحة كقراءة سعيد

BURHAN:v4p334/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p334/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p334/r10.claim: When a predicate precedes inna, the lām can attach to the fronted phrase; the underlying order is ‘they wander in their intoxication.’
BURHAN:v4p334/r10.anchor: أو على ما يتصل بالخبر إذا تقدم عليه

FARRA:v3p232/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r10.claim: The Fire is the abode of the people just characterized in the passage.

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r1.claim: The phrase may mean هي المأوى له, or مأواه with أل substituting for the possessive pronoun; the latter is the Kufan position.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r1.anchor: هي المأوى له، أو هي مأواه، وقامت أل مقام الضمير، وهو رأي الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r2.claim: One of those analyses must supply the predicate's link back to the subject; omitting an overt link is eased by the phrase's position at a verse ending.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r2.anchor: ولا بد من أحد هذين التأويلين في الآية الكريمة لأجل العائد من الجملة الواقعة خبرا إلى المبتدأ. والذي حسن عدم ذكر العائد كون الكلمة وقعت رأس فاصلة

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r3.claim: A cited poem combines أل with a possessive pronoun, which would be unexpected if أل replaced that pronoun; the author uses it against the Kufan account.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r3.anchor: رحيب قطاب الجيب منها رفيقة بجس الندامى بضة المتجرد إذا لو كانت أل عوضا من الضمير لما جمع بينهما في هذا البيت

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses it as the transgressor's abode, comparing it to غض الطرف: possession is understood, not replaced by أل, and both things are definite by context.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والمعنى: فإن الجحيم مأواه

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r5.claim: The Shaykh objects that al-Zamakhshari supplies no link to the subject: he rejects the Kufan view and does not posit the pronoun that Basrans posit.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r5.anchor: وهو كلام لا يتحصل منه الرابط العائد على المبتدأ، إذ قد نفى مذهب الكوفيين، ولم يقدر ضميرا كما قدره البصريون

SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r6.claim: The author answers that al-Zamakhshari's appeal to what is understood is exactly the Basran analysis, and questions how the Shaykh missed this.
SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r6.anchor: قوله: " ولكن لما علم " إلى آخره هو عين قول البصريين، ولا أدري كيف خفي عليه هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers taking the response to إذا as the clause beginning فأما; Alusi considers this sound and says the syntax is straightforward if the preceding clause is conditional.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1.anchor: جواب إذا على أنها شرطية لا ظرفية كما جوز على طريقة قوله تعالى فأما يأتينكم مني هدى الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.claim: Alternatively, the response to إذا is omitted and the تفصيل clause explains it; other suggestions derive the omission from what precedes or follows, which Alusi finds unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2.anchor: وقيل جوابها محذوف كأنه قيل فإذا جاءت وقع ما لا يدخل تحت الوصف وقوله سبحانه فأما الخ تفصيل لذلك المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r1.claim: The Kufans treat the article in al-maʾwā as replacing the possessor’s pronoun, yielding ‘his refuge’; Basrans instead understand ‘the refuge for him.’ The omitted possessor is obvious, and the ending suits the rhyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r1.anchor: أي مأواه على ما رآه الكوفيون من أن ألأفي مثله عوض عن المضاف إليه الضمير وبها يحصل الربط

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r2.claim: Alusi says هي is either a separative pronoun or a subject referring to Hell; the clause then restricts refuge to Hell alone. Al-Zamakhsharī chooses the latter explanation of the omitted possessor.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r2.anchor: وهي أما ضمير فصل لا محل له من الإعراب أو ضمير جهنم مبتدأ والكلام دال على الحصر

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r5.claim: Maʾwā is a place one seeks for refuge, protection, and residence.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r5.anchor: والمأوى: المكان يؤوى إليه ويلاذ ويسكن فيه

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r6.claim: The Qur'an uses maʾwā only for the afterlife, with Paradise or with Hell and its other names; this presents the afterlife as the permanent abode and final destination.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r6.anchor: وهو صنيع يشهد بأن القرآن الكريم يقرر أن الدار الآخرة هي المأوى

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r7.claim: The verb awā occurs fourteen times in the Qur'an and consistently conveys safety, protection, or refuge, as in the examples cited.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r7.anchor: فيأتي في القرآن أربع عشرة مرة، لا يخطئ الحس فيها جميعاً، معنى المأمن والحمى والملاذ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r1.claim: Hell is the abode for the transgressor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج أي هي المأوى له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats this as the answer to the clause if the Overwhelming Event comes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r2.anchor: وهذا جواب فإذا جاءت الطامة فإن الأمر كذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r1.claim: The Fire is the place of return.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r2.claim: He contrasts this with the abode of the one who fears his Lord's standing and restrains his soul from desire.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r2.anchor: ﴿ وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى ﴿ سورة عبس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r3.speaker: الكوفيين
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r3.claim: The Kufans take the definite article as a substitute for a possessive construction.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r3.anchor: والألف واللام بدل من الاضافة وهذا عند الكوفيين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r4.speaker: سيبويه والبصريين
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r4.claim: Sibawayh and the Basrans understand it as “the place of refuge for him.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r4.anchor: وعند سيبويه وعند البصريين هى المأوى له
